text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on February 25 in history.
1308 - The coronation of Edward II of England took place.
1570 - Pope Pius V issued the papal bull Regnans in Excelsis, excommunicating Queen Elizabeth I of England.
1707 - Carlo Goldoni, Italian dramatist and playwright who wrote over 250 plays, born.
1723 - Sir Christopher Wren, English architect and designer, died. He became a prolific designer of buildings following the Great Fire of London in 1666, notably of the new St Paul's cathedral.
1778 - Jose de San Martin, Argentine revolutionary leader and national hero, born. He played a big part in achieving independence for Chile and Peru.
1841 - Pierre Auguste Renoir, French Impressionist painter, born. He continued painting late in life despite being crippled with arthritis.
1841 - Explorer Edward John Eyre left Fowlers Bay in South Australia on an overland trip around the Great Australian Bight. He reached Albany in July.
1873 - Enrico Caruso, Italian operatic tenor, born. The power and purity of his voice coupled with his acting ability made him one of the greatest tenors of all time.
1888 - John Foster Dulles, U.S. diplomat and Secretary of State, born.
1890 - Dame Myra Hess, English concert pianist, born.

1899 - Paul Julius Reuter, German founder of the news agency that bears his name, died. In 1850 he set up a pigeon post service from Aachen to London to bridge the last gap in the expanding European telegraph system.
1901 - Zeppo, youngest of the Marx Brothers comedy team, born.
1914 - Sir John Tenniel, English artist and illustrator of "Alice in Wonderland", died.
1917 - Anthony Burgess, British novelist, author of "A Clockwork Orange", born as John Burgess Wilson.
1941 - David Puttnam, British film producer and Oscar winner for "Chariots of Fire", born.

1948 - In Czechoslovakia, President Edvard Benes accepted the resignations of non-Communists from his cabinet. The Communists legally took control of the government in what was called the "February Coup".
1956 - In a sensational speech to the Communist Party Congress, Nikita Khrushchev denounced Stalin as a demigod and tyrant.
1964 - Cassius Clay (Muhammad Ali) became world heavyweight boxing champion for the first time after he knocked out Sonny Liston in Miami.
1972 - President Kenneth Kaunda announced his cabinet's decision to impose a one-party state in Zambia.
1972 - The Soviet Union's Luna 20 spacecraft returned to Earth with samples of the Moon's surface.
1983 - Tennesee Williams, U.S. playwright notable for "A Streetcar Named Desire", died.
1993 - Kim Young-sam was sworn in as South Korea's first civilian president for 32 years.
1994 - Baruch Goldstein, a Jewish settler, massacred 43 Moslem worshippers at a Hebron mosque. He was beaten to death at the scene.
1994 - Malaysia banned British firms from government contracts following British media stories alleging corrupt business dealings.
1994 - The U.S. expelled Russian diplomat Aleksandr Iosifovich Lysenko, identified as Moscow's chief intelligence officer in Washington.
1995 - North Korea's defence minister O Jin-u, number two man in North Korea's ruling hierarchy, died of cancer.
1996 - Moslem bombers killed 25 people and wounded 77 in two revenge attacks in Israel.
